However, it's essential to closely analyze each AC against the details of the test case. In this instance, while several ACs are indeed addressed, there is one specific AC regarding redirecting work to another instructor that is not covered in the scenario. This discrepancy highlights the importance of carefully reviewing both test cases and acceptance criteria to ensure comprehensive coverage in testing. Understanding this distinction will enhance your ability to evaluate scenarios effectively and strengthen your skills in identifying gaps in testing processes. Keep up the great work in honing your analytical skills!
b) AC1, AC2, AC3, AC5 are not covered" is incorrect because it implies that only those specific acceptance criteria are excluded from coverage, but that isn't the case. Each acceptance criterion must be evaluated against the provided test scenarios. In this situation, while you may think some ACs are not covered, the evidence suggests that there are additional criteria (like AC5) specifically lacking validation. It’s important to thoroughly check all acceptance criteria to ensure comprehensive testing. This way, you strengthen your ability to assess which aspects of a project need further evaluation, reinforcing your understanding of effective testing practices. Keep exploring these aspects for deeper learning!
c) AC1, AC5 are not covered" is incorrect because it assumes that these specific acceptance criteria are entirely omitted from the test case, which may not reflect the actual situation. In evaluating acceptance criteria, it’s crucial to review all of them against the test scenarios carefully. Instead of looking at just a couple of criteria, consider how many of the acceptance criteria are addressed as a whole. This will help you better understand what is included and what requires more attention. Keep practicing this analytical approach, as it’ll enhance your ability to assess the completeness of testing and improve your skills in software development!

questions.text: What is the primary goal of using brainstorming in collaborative user story writing?
options: a) To finalize the technical specifications of the user stories
b) To generate a wide range of ideas from all team members
c) To allocate tasks among the development team
d) To document the user stories in the project management software
questions.explanation:
a) To finalize the technical specifications of the user stories" is incorrect because brainstorming is primarily focused on generating diverse ideas rather than finalizing details. The goal of brainstorming is to gather insights and contributions from all team members, encouraging creativity and collaboration. In user story writing, this collaborative approach allows for a richer and more comprehensive understanding of user needs and requirements, rather than simply specifying technical aspects. Keep exploring how brainstorming can enhance team collaboration and storytelling in user stories!
c) To allocate tasks among the development team" is incorrect because the primary aim of brainstorming in collaborative user story writing is to generate and share ideas, not to assign specific tasks. While task allocation is important in development, it occurs after brainstorming once the ideas are generated and clarified. Brainstorming fosters open communication and creative input from all team members, ensuring that user stories are comprehensive and meet user needs, rather than simply focusing on how tasks will be divided among individuals. Keep exploring how collaboration enhances the writing process!
d) To document the user stories in the project management software" is incorrect because the primary purpose of brainstorming is to generate ideas and collaboratively develop user stories, rather than simply documenting them. While documentation is important, it comes after the brainstorming process, where team members contribute and refine their understanding of user needs. Brainstorming focuses on creativity and collaboration, ensuring the user stories are comprehensive before they are formally recorded in any software. Keep engaging with these concepts to enhance your understanding of effective user story development!

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT the PRIMARY benefit of using acceptance criteria?
options: a) Serve as a basis for the user story acceptance testing
b) Allow accurate planning and estimation
c) Get rid of contracts by replacing them with live communication with the customer
d) Define the scope of the user story
questions.explanation:
a) Serve as a basis for the user story acceptance testing" is incorrect because, while acceptance criteria do indeed serve this purpose, the question specifically asks for the option that is NOT a PRIMARY benefit. The primary benefits of acceptance criteria focus more on ensuring clarity, scope definition, and facilitating effective communication among stakeholders rather than just testing. It's important to understand that acceptance criteria have multiple uses, but the question is about distinguishing between primary and secondary benefits. Keep exploring the different aspects of acceptance criteria to deepen your understanding!
b) Allow accurate planning and estimation" is incorrect because while accurate planning and estimation are important aspects of project management, they are not the primary focus of acceptance criteria. Acceptance criteria primarily serve to define what it means for a user story to be complete and ensure everyone has a shared understanding of the requirements. They help clarify scope and expectations among stakeholders rather than directly influencing planning or estimation processes. This distinction is key to understanding the role of acceptance criteria in agile methodologies. Keep exploring these concepts to enhance your grasp of user story development!
d) Define the scope of the user story" is incorrect because while defining the scope is an important part of user story development, brainstorming is primarily about generating a variety of ideas and perspectives among team members. This collaborative environment encourages innovative thoughts and creativity that contribute to user story creation, rather than focusing on the final scope itself. It’s essential to recognize that brainstorming happens early in the process and is aimed at gathering input before definitive decisions about scope are made. Keep exploring this concept to deepen your understanding of the collaborative nature of user story writing!

questions.text:
Consider the following user story:
• As a shopper, I want the ability to purchase products on the website so that I can acquire the items I desire
Acceptance Criteria:
• AC1: Users can purchase a maximum of 5 products in a single transaction
• AC2: Users can apply one of the following coupon codes at checkout:
   - 'Saver5' for a 5% discount
   - 'Super10' for a 10% discount
   - 'Mega15' for a 15% discount
• AC3: If a user purchases exactly 5 products, a 'Bulk Buy Discount' of 10% is automatically applied to their order
• AC4: Coupons and automatic discounts cannot be combined. The system applies the highest applicable discount
You are using acceptance test-driven development (ATDD) to design test cases for this user story. Which of the following test cases would logically be the first to be created and run to test AC4?
options: a) Title: Multiple Discounts Not Applied Input: User adds 5 items (triggering the 'Bulk Buy Discount') and attempts to apply the 'Super10' coupon. Expected Output: System applies the 'Bulk Buy Discount' (10%) and displays a message indicating that multiple discounts cannot be combined.

b) Title: Product Purchase Limit Enforced Input: User adds 4 products, applies the 'Saver5' coupon, and attempts to add a 5th and 6th product. Expected Output: System prevents adding more than 5 products and displays a clear error message

c) Title: Higher Discount Prevails (Dynamic Change) Input: User adds 5 products (triggering the 'Bulk Buy Discount') and applies the 'Mega15' coupon. They then remove one product Expected Output: System continues to apply the 'Mega15' coupon (15%)

d) Title: Higher Discount Prevails (Initial Coupon) Input: User adds 3 products and applies the 'Mega15' coupon. User adds 2 more products to reach the 'Bulk Buy Discount' threshold. Expected Output: System continues to apply the 'Mega15' coupon (15%).
questions.explanation:
b) Title: Product Purchase Limit Enforced" is incorrect because this test case does not address the specific focus of AC4, which deals with how the system should handle discount applications, not purchase limits. AC4 emphasizes the logic of applying the highest applicable discount when multiple options are available. By concentrating on a different aspect of user stories, in this case, you're missing the opportunity to verify essential functionality around discount handling and prioritization. It's important to align test cases with the corresponding acceptance criteria to ensure all requirements are properly validated. Keep practicing to strengthen your understanding of how to connect test cases with acceptance criteria effectively!
c) Title: Higher Discount Prevails (Dynamic Change)" is incorrect because it focuses on verifying that an existing discount (the 'Mega15' coupon) remains valid when the number of products in the cart changes. However, this specific scenario does not adequately check if the system is correctly applying the highest discount from all available options, particularly in relation to the 'Bulk Buy Discount.'
When you remove a product, it may not trigger a comparison with the bulk discount criteria at all, which means it's not fully testing the logic required to ensure the best discount is applied. The goal is to ensure that the system evaluates and selects the highest applicable discount, which needs to be directly addressed in your test case. Understanding this distinction will help you improve your focus on the essence of acceptance criteria and craft more precise test cases in future scenarios. Keep exploring this concept to deepen your expertise!
a) is incorrect because it focuses on a negative scenario—where multiple discounts are not combined. While this situation is important to test, it may not be the best starting point for verifying overall functionality. The learning objective here emphasizes understanding how to assess discount applications effectively.
By initiating with a negative case, you might overlook essential aspects of the system's core functionality, such as ensuring the highest discount is applied under typical conditions. Additionally, the acceptance criteria do not clearly define how to handle scenarios with equal discounts, making your selected scenario less ideal for confirming the desired behavior.
Taking a balanced approach to your test case design can significantly enhance your testing efficacy. Keep up the good work and continue to refine your understanding of how to create effective test cases!

questions.text: Which collaborative technique is recommended for achieving a shared vision during the authorship of a user story?
options: a) Using project management tools to track changes
b) Conducting formal stakeholder interviews periodically
c) Employing brainstorming and mind-mapping techniques
d) Outsourcing part of the writing process to external consultants
questions.explanation:
a) Using project management tools to track changes is more focused on organizing and documenting progress rather than actively engaging team members in the creative process. While these tools can be useful for managing projects, they do not inherently facilitate the collaborative brainstorming and idea generation necessary for achieving a shared vision in writing user stories. Effective collaboration in this context requires techniques that encourage participation, creativity, and diverse input from all team members. Engaging in methods that foster open dialogue and collective brainstorming is key to developing a cohesive understanding of what needs to be achieved in a user story, which tracking changes alone does not accomplish. Keep exploring effective collaboration techniques to enhance your understanding and skills!
b) Conducting formal stakeholder interviews periodically can provide valuable insights and information; however, it does not actively foster the collaborative, creative atmosphere needed for crafting a shared vision of user stories. This technique tends to be more structured and may not encourage the level of interaction and idea generation that brainstorming and mind-mapping foster. User stories benefit from a dynamic, collective approach where all team members contribute ideas freely. By using techniques that invite diverse participation, you can better achieve a comprehensive understanding of the user story's goals, which is essential for successful collaboration. Keep exploring methods that encourage collaboration to enhance your skills in developing effective user stories!
d) Outsourcing part of the writing process to external consultants is not conducive to achieving a shared vision among your team. While consultants can provide expertise, relying on them can create a disconnect between the writing process and the collaborative efforts of your team. User stories require input from all stakeholders to ensure that everyone’s perspectives and insights are considered, fostering a common understanding. Engaging directly in the creative process through collaborative methods promotes ownership and aligns the team towards a unified goal, which outsourcing does not facilitate. Emphasizing in-house collaboration helps you build a stronger, shared vision essential for your project's success. Keep exploring ways to enhance teamwork and idea generation!

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a typical characteristic of well-written acceptance criteria?
options: a) Defines the scope of the user story
b) Serve as a basis for tests of the Q1 and Q4 testing quadrants rather than the Q2 and Q3
c) Serve as a basis for the user story acceptance testing
d) Agreed upon by stakeholders
questions.explanation:
a) Defines the scope of the user story" is incorrect because, while defining the scope is indeed important, this characteristic does not directly pertain to acceptance criteria. Acceptance criteria are specific conditions that must be met for a user story to be considered complete, focusing on measurable outcomes and success benchmarks rather than merely establishing the boundaries of the story. Understanding this distinction will help you grasp the essence of what makes acceptance criteria effective in guiding the testing and validation processes. Keep exploring the nuances of user story elements to enhance your skills!
c) Serve as a basis for the user story acceptance testing" is incorrect because while acceptance criteria do support testing, they should primarily focus on defining clear conditions under which a user story is deemed complete. Specifically, establishing criteria based on device types and browsers, while useful for comprehensive testing, does not enhance the direct measurement of key performance indicators like speed and responsiveness for individual scenarios. Acceptance criteria should instead concentrate on what the user expects from the functionality in a specific context, helping the development and testing teams understand the desired outcomes better.
Understanding this nuance will help you refine your approach to writing effective acceptance criteria, so keep engaging with the material to strengthen your grasp on the topic!
d) Agreed upon by stakeholders" is incorrect because, while stakeholder agreement is essential for defining acceptance criteria, it does not directly address what makes criteria effective in measuring success. Acceptance criteria focus on specific conditions or outcomes that need to be met for a user story to be considered complete, such as performance metrics or functionality requirements. Simply stating that criteria are agreed upon does not provide the actionable specifics necessary for testing and validation. It's important to ensure that acceptance criteria include measurable and testable elements to guide both development and verification processes effectively. Keep exploring the distinction between collaboration and clear expectations; it's a key aspect of mastering acceptance criteria!

questions.text:
Consider the following user story:
• As a frequent traveler, I want to receive notifications about flight delays, cancellations, or gate changes via my preferred method (email or SMS), so I can adjust my plans accordingly
And its acceptance criteria:
• AC1. The user can subscribe to flight notifications by entering their flight number, date, and preferred notification method (email or SMS)
• AC2. The user must provide a valid email address (if email is selected) or a valid mobile phone number (if SMS is selected)
• AC3. The user should select the timeframe in which they want to receive notifications (48 hours before departure or 24 hours before departure)
• AC4. The system will send a notification to the user's chosen method if the flight status changes to "delayed" or canceled"
• AC5. The user can change their preferred notification method at any time by repeating steps 1-3
• AC6. The user can unsubscribe from notifications immediately after initial subscribing or after changing their notification method
Which of the following test cases will NOT be relevant for this user story?
options: a) Input: The customer enters a valid flight number, selects SMS as the notification method, and chooses notifications to be sent 48 hours before departure Expected Output: The system confirms the subscription and sends a notification via SMS if there is any change in the flight status
b) Input: The customer logs into their account to review past flights they have taken with the airline Expected Output: The system displays a list of past flight bookings and their details

c) Input: The user updates their notification method from SMS to email and selects to receive notifications 24 hours before departure Expected Output: The system updates the user's preferences and confirms the change
d) Input: The user receives an SMS notification for a gate change and then immediately unsubscribes from further notifications
questions.explanation:
a) Input: The customer enters a valid flight number, selects SMS as the notification method, and chooses notifications to be sent 48 hours before departure..." is incorrect because this test case is relevant to the user story, which emphasizes receiving notifications about flight status changes. This scenario aligns with the acceptance criteria, as it depicts a process where the user subscribes to notifications, capturing key aspects of the system's expected behavior.
It's important to focus on how each test case relates to the core functionality described in the user story and acceptance criteria. Think about each scenario's direct tie to the main goal of the user story, which is centered on real-time notifications for flights rather than tangential actions. Keep exploring these connections, and it will enhance your understanding of how to identify relevant test cases effectively!
c) Input: The user updates their notification method from SMS to email and selects to receive notifications 24 hours before departure. Expected Output: The system updates the user's preferences and confirms the change" is incorrect because this scenario is indeed related to the user story about receiving notifications for flight updates. The focus of the user story is on how users can customize their notification preferences, and this option exemplifies that by showing a user adjusting their notification method, which is a key aspect of the overall functionality being tested.
Understanding how test cases align with the core objectives of the user story is crucial. This particular scenario demonstrates the system's expected behavior when a user modifies their preferences, which is directly connected to the acceptance criteria. Keep exploring these connections; identifying how test cases relate to user needs will strengthen your grasp of effective testing practices!
d) Input: The user receives an SMS notification for a gate change and then immediately unsubscribes from further notifications. Expected Output: The system processes the unsubscription and confirms that no further notifications will be sent" is incorrect because this scenario still relates closely to the user story about receiving notifications.
Though the focus is on unsubscribing, this action occurs directly after receiving a notification, highlighting the system's responsiveness to user preferences and behavior. It captures an essential aspect of how users interact with the notification system, which is crucial for understanding overall functionality.
Recognizing the importance of user actions related to notifications helps you better understand how acceptance criteria are framed. This scenario reflects how the system needs to process changes in user preferences, which is relevant when discussing the full user experience. Keep exploring these connections, and you'll continue to strengthen your grasp of effective test case identification!

questions.text:
Consider this acceptance criterion for a user story on a music streaming app:
• Given the user is on a song's page
• When the user clicks on the "Play" button
• Then the song should start playing
• And the "Play" button should change to a "Pause" button
Which format best describes this acceptance criterion?
options: a) Rule-oriented
b) Scenario-oriented
c) User interface-focused
d) Data validation-oriented
questions.explanation:
a) Rule-oriented" is incorrect because this acceptance criterion follows a scenario-oriented format, which is structured using the Given/When/Then approach. This format effectively describes a specific situation that the system should respond to, allowing for clear testing of functionality based on user interactions.
In a rule-oriented format, you would typically see a list of conditions or rules without specifying the context in which they apply, which differs from the detailed scenario provided here. Understanding the distinction between these formats is essential for accurately communicating system behavior and ensuring that acceptance criteria are structured effectively for testing purposes. Keep exploring these concepts, and you'll continue to improve your understanding of acceptance criteria!
c) User interface-focused" is incorrect because the Given/When/Then approach is not primarily concerned with user interface elements but rather with user scenarios and their interactions with the system. This method details the context of a specific situation, capturing what happens when a user takes an action, rather than focusing on how the interface itself looks or functions. It's important to understand that acceptance criteria written in this format are meant to guide testing by articulating behavior and expected outcomes in a narrative way. Recognizing this distinction will enhance your ability to identify and create effective acceptance criteria. Keep up your learning, and you'll strengthen your understanding further!
d) Data validation-oriented" is incorrect because the Given/When/Then format does not specifically focus on validating data alone. Instead, it is designed to describe user interactions within a scenario, outlining conditions and expected outcomes based on those interactions. While data validation can be a part of a larger scenario, the approach itself is more about capturing the flow of actions from a user perspective. Understanding this distinction will help you better recognize how different criteria formats serve specific purposes in acceptance criteria discussions. Keep up the great work in exploring these concepts!

questions.text:
Consider the following user story and acceptance criteria:
• As a student, I want to submit my homework through the online learning platform so that I can receive feedback from my instructors
Acceptance Criteria:
• AC1: Students must be able to upload their homework assignments directly to the platform
• AC2: If instructors are satisfied with the quality of the homework, they should be able to approve it and assign grades through the platform
• AC3: If instructors are not satisfied with the quality of the homework, they must be able to request revisions from students and provide comments
• AC4: Students must be able to resubmit their homework after making the required revisions
• AC5: Instructors must be able to redirect the work to another instructor by changing the assignee in the system
Which of the following is the BEST example of an ATDD test for this user story?
options: a) Test if a student is able to resubmit their homework after making the required revisions if the instructor assigns a lower grade to the homework. Expected result: The homework is successfully resubmitted, and the system confirms the resubmission to both the student and the instructor

b) Test if a student can reassign their homework to another instructor if the first instructor hasn't reviewed it within 3 days. Expected result: The homework is successfully reassigned to another instructor
c) Test if an instructor, upon reviewing a homework submission, can request revisions by providing specific feedback. Expected result: The student receives the feedback and knows to resubmit
d) Test if a student receives a notification when their homework is graded as 'A'. Expected result: The student views their grade on the platform
questions.explanation:
a) is not correct because it introduces a condition about the instructor assigning a lower grade, which is not specified in the acceptance criteria provided. While it may seem realistic to consider grades in that context, focusing solely on the requirement for resubmission after revisions is essential for aligning with the acceptance criteria. The main goal is to test the functionality accurately as outlined in the user story. This approach emphasizes understanding exactly what needs to be tested based on the criteria given, which allows for effective verification of user interactions and system behavior. Keep up the great work as you refine your understanding of how to create precise tests based on specified requirements!
b) is not correct because it introduces a new functionality—allowing students to reassign homework to another instructor—that is not covered in the original acceptance criteria. The criteria focus on the student submitting their homework and the instructor's role in providing feedback. By adding the concept of reassigning homework, the scenario deviates from the established roles and responsibilities outlined in the criteria. Focusing on the specific actions that align with the acceptance criteria ensures that you're testing what is explicitly required, which is a crucial skill in developing effective user stories. Keep up your engagement with these concepts; it’s great that you’re seeking clarity!
d) Test if a student receives a notification when their homework is graded as 'A'" is incorrect because the acceptance criteria do not specifically state that there will be automatic notifications for grades. The criteria primarily focus on the submission of homework and the resulting grade displayed on the platform. It's essential to stick to what is explicitly mentioned in the criteria when developing tests to ensure clarity and accuracy in what you're evaluating. This approach helps you align your testing with the documented expectations without introducing assumptions that could lead to misunderstandings. Keep engaging with these concepts, as refining your understanding will strengthen your ability to develop clear and effective acceptance criteria!

questions.text:
Consider this acceptance criterion for a user story on a social media platform:
• Given a user is viewing their profile
• When the user clicks on the "Edit Profile" button
• Then the profile fields should become editable
Which format best describes this acceptance criterion?
options: a) Rule-oriented
b) Checklist-based
c) Scenario-oriented
d) Table-based
questions.explanation:
a) Rule-oriented" is incorrect because this format involves presenting rules through lists or tables, focusing on explicit conditions. However, the acceptance criterion you provided uses a "Given/When/Then" structure, which describes a specific scenario that illustrates the user interaction. This narrative format enables you to visualize how an action leads to a result, making it more aligned with user experiences. Understanding the distinction between these formats will help you better grasp how to frame acceptance criteria for user stories. Keep up the great work in exploring these concepts!
b) Checklist-based" is incorrect because this format typically involves a simple list of items or conditions that need to be checked off, focusing on completion rather than narrating interactions. In contrast, the Given/When/Then structure is designed to describe specific user interactions and expected outcomes in a scenario-based way. This makes it more effective for clarifying user experiences and guiding development. Understanding this distinction is important for effectively framing acceptance criteria in user stories. Keep exploring these concepts; your curiosity is an excellent way to enhance your learning!
d) Table-based" is incorrect because this format typically organizes information into rows and columns for easy comparison and reference. However, the Given/When/Then framework is narrative and scenario-driven, focusing on descriptions of actions and expected results rather than merely presenting data. This distinction is crucial for understanding how to create acceptance criteria that capture user interactions. It's great that you're engaging with these concepts—continue exploring to deepen your understanding!

questions.text:
Consider the following user story:
• As a shopper, I want the ability to purchase products on the website so that I can acquire the items I desire
Acceptance Criteria:
• AC1: Users can apply one of the following coupon codes at checkout:
• 'Saver5' for a 5% discount
• 'Super10' for a 10% discount
• 'Mega15' for a 15% discount
• AC2: If a user purchases exactly 5 products, a 'Bulk Buy Discount' of 10% is automatically applied to their order
• AC3: Coupons and automatic discounts cannot be combined. The system applies the highest applicable discount
• AC4: If a user removes items from their cart causing the 'Bulk Buy Discount' to no longer apply, the automatic discount should be removed
Which of the following is NOT a valid test scenario based on the user story and acceptance criteria?
options: a) Add four products to the cart and apply the 'Super10' coupon code. Result: The system applies only the 10% discount from the 'Super10' coupon
b) Add five products to the cart and do not apply any coupon code: The system automatically applies the 'Bulk Buy Discount' of 10%, and the final price reflects this discount
c) Add five products to the cart and enter the 'Mega15' coupon code. Result: The system applies only the 15% discount from the 'Mega15' coupon, ignoring the 'Bulk Buy Discount'
d) Add five products to the cart and enter the 'Superb20' coupon code. Result: The system doesn't apply the discount and shows the error message
questions.explanation:
a) Add four products to the cart and apply the 'Super10' coupon code. Result: The system applies only the 10% discount from the 'Super10' coupon," is incorrect because of the way discounts are applied according to the acceptance criteria. Specifically, here, the condition states that if a user does not meet the requirement of purchasing exactly five products, the 'Bulk Buy Discount' does not trigger.
In this case, since you only added four products, only the coupon discount should apply. However, by stating that the system applies the 10% discount from the coupon, it does not account for the fact that the 'Bulk Buy Discount' would not apply in this situation. Therefore, the testing scenario here conflates two acceptance criteria that essentially check what should happen when the discount conditions are not met. Understanding these criteria is key to creating valid test scenarios and seeing how they interact in different situations. Keep analyzing these details; it's a great way to sharpen your testing skills!
b) Add five products to the cart and do not apply any coupon code: The system automatically applies the 'Bulk Buy Discount' of 10%, and the final price reflects this discount" is not correct because it assumes that the bulk discount applies without any action from you, which is not aligned with the acceptance criteria.
The criteria specify that the bulk discount will activate based on the quantity of products added, requiring you to actively verify that condition. This means that simply adding five products and not applying a coupon doesn’t automatically ensure that the discount will be applied just because five items are there. Instead, it is essential to check how the bulk discount functions under the acceptance criteria, which involves understanding its specific conditions for application.
This scenario helps you grasp the importance of clearly defining conditions and expected outcomes in test cases, reinforcing how to create accurate and effective testing scenarios. Keep practicing, as this will enhance your understanding of acceptance criteria and how they guide testing processes!
c) Add five products to the cart and enter the 'Mega15' coupon code. Result: The system applies only the 15% discount from the 'Mega15' coupon, ignoring the 'Bulk Buy Discount'" is incorrect because it overlooks an important aspect of the discount rules. The acceptance criteria indicate that the system should compare discount values and apply the highest discount available.
By just considering the coupon discount, this choice doesn't align with the requirement to check for the bulk buy discount as well, which is potentially a greater benefit in this scenario. It’s important to understand that the purpose of such criteria is to ensure that the testing validates that the system correctly identifies which discount is more advantageous for the customer.
This understanding helps you appreciate how to properly assess conditions and results when applying multiple discounts, enhancing your overall testing proficiency. Keep up the great work in measuring your understanding of acceptance criteria and their implications!
